title: The Quiet Page: Reading on E‑Ink in a Loud World
author: Ada Example
summary: A short essay about slow reading.
html_content:
The Quiet Page

There’s a particular kind of silence that only paper makes — or, lately, e‑ink. It doesn’t glow; it waits.

“Read slowly,” my teacher said, “and the book will read you back.” I didn’t understand her until years later.

Why slow matters

Speed is a habit, not a virtue. When we skim, we keep the shape of an argument and lose its texture — the small turns of phrase that make a writer worth reading.

Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.

Simone Weil wrote that in a letter, and it’s been quoted so often it’s almost lost its edges. Almost.

  • Turn off notifications.
  • Pick one long piece a day.
  • Write in the margins, even if it’s just a single word.

None of this is new. It’s just easier to forget than it used to be.
